questions.stem: Which method of asexual reproduction is used by Amoeba?
questions.explanation: In binary fission the nucleus divides by mitosis and the whole cell then splits into two roughly equal daughter cells, each a complete organism. It is the fastest form of reproduction known, which is why bacteria and protists can multiply so rapidly.

distractorRationale.a: In budding the new individual grows as a small outgrowth, as in yeast and Hydra
distractorRationale.c: Spore formation is used by fungi and ferns
distractorRationale.d: Vegetative propagation involves plant organs such as tubers and rhizomes

questions.stem: Ginger is propagated naturally by means of a
questions.explanation: A rhizome is a swollen horizontal stem that grows just below the soil surface, with buds along it that send up new shoots and roots. Ginger and canna lily grow this way, and each piece with a bud can become a new plant.

distractorRationale.a: A bulb is a short vertical stem with fleshy leaves, as in onion and garlic
distractorRationale.c: A sucker arises from the base of an above-ground stem, as in banana and pineapple
distractorRationale.d: A stem tuber is a rounded swollen stem tip, as in Irish potato

questions.stem: Offspring produced by asexual reproduction are genetically identical to the parent because

options.text: they are produced by mitosis, with no gametes and no fertilisation
they are produced by meiosis, which halves the chromosome number
crossing over occurs during their formation
two parents contribute equal numbers of chromosomes

questions.explanation: Mitosis copies every chromosome exactly and separates the copies, so each daughter cell receives the same alleles as the parent. Because no gametes are formed there is no meiosis, no crossing over and no mixing of two genomes, which is why the offspring are clones.

distractorRationale.b: Meiosis is used in sexual reproduction and produces genetically different cells
distractorRationale.c: Crossing over happens in meiosis and is a source of variation
distractorRationale.d: Asexual reproduction has only one parent

questions.stem: A farmer plants a whole field with cuttings taken from one high-yielding cassava plant. What is the greatest risk of doing this?

options.text: The plants will grow too slowly
The plants are genetically identical, so a single disease could destroy the entire field
The plants will not produce any tubers
The plants will need pollinating insects

questions.explanation: Cuttings are clones, so every plant has exactly the same alleles and therefore exactly the same weaknesses. If a pathogen can infect one, none of the others has any genetic resistance to slow the outbreak, and the whole crop may be lost.

distractorRationale.a: Vegetative propagation usually gives faster establishment than seed
distractorRationale.c: Cassava grown from cuttings produces tubers normally; this is standard practice
distractorRationale.d: Cuttings need no pollination at all, which is one of the advantages

questions.stem: Fertilisation is best defined as the

options.text: transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma
fusion of a male gamete nucleus with a female gamete nucleus to form a zygote
division of a zygote into many cells
release of gametes into the surrounding water

questions.explanation: Fertilisation is the actual fusion of the two haploid nuclei, which restores the diploid number and creates a new individual with a unique combination of alleles. Everything before it — pollination or the release of gametes — merely brings the gametes together.

distractorRationale.a: Pollen transfer is pollination, which precedes fertilisation and may not lead to it
distractorRationale.c: Division of the zygote is cleavage, part of development after fertilisation
distractorRationale.d: Releasing gametes is spawning; the gametes must still meet and fuse

questions.stem: Yeast reproduces asexually by
questions.explanation: A small outgrowth or bud appears on the surface of the parent yeast cell, its nucleus divides by mitosis and one nucleus passes into the bud, which then enlarges and eventually separates. Unlike binary fission, the two cells produced are unequal in size.

distractorRationale.b: Fragmentation occurs in filamentous organisms such as Spirogyra
distractorRationale.c: In binary fission the parent splits into two equal parts, which is not what yeast does
distractorRationale.d: Layering is an artificial method of propagating plants

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of sexual reproduction over asexual reproduction?

options.text: It is faster and needs only one parent
It produces variation, so some offspring may survive a change in the environment
It guarantees that offspring inherit the parent's exact qualities
It produces offspring that always stay close to the parent

questions.explanation: Meiosis and the random fusion of gametes give every offspring a different combination of alleles, so a population is unlikely to be wiped out by a single new disease or a change in climate. That variation is also what makes natural selection and selective breeding possible.

distractorRationale.a: Speed and needing only one parent are advantages of asexual reproduction
distractorRationale.c: Exact inheritance of parental qualities is a feature of asexual reproduction
distractorRationale.d: Seeds and fruits are usually dispersed away from the parent, which is itself an advantage

questions.stem: Gametes are produced by meiosis, so each gamete contains half the chromosome number of the parent cell.
questions.explanation: True. Meiosis separates the members of every homologous pair, so a gamete is haploid. This is essential, because the fusion of two haploid gametes at fertilisation then restores exactly the diploid number rather than doubling it.

questions.stem: A gardener grafts a scion from a sweet orange variety onto the rootstock of a vigorous, disease-resistant citrus. The fruit produced will

options.text: be a mixture of the qualities of both plants
have the qualities of the scion, because the fruit develops from scion tissue
have the qualities of the rootstock
be sterile and produce no seeds

questions.explanation: Grafting joins two plants but does not mix their genes; the scion keeps its own genotype and produces flowers and fruit typical of its variety. The rootstock contributes its root system, and so its vigour and disease resistance, but not its fruit characteristics.

distractorRationale.a: Grafting is a physical union, not a genetic cross, so no blending occurs
distractorRationale.c: The rootstock does not bear the fruit, so its fruit qualities are irrelevant
distractorRationale.d: Grafted citrus fruits and seeds develop normally

questions.stem: State four differences between asexual and sexual reproduction, and give two advantages and one disadvantage of propagating crops vegetatively.
markingGuide: Any four differences, one mark each: number of parents (one versus two); gametes absent versus present; fertilisation absent versus present; division by mitosis versus meiosis then mitosis; offspring identical versus varied; usually faster versus slower
Advantage 1: offspring are genetically identical to the parent, so a proven high-yielding or disease-resistant variety is reproduced exactly (2 marks)

Advantage 2: it is faster and the plants mature or bear sooner than seedlings; accept also that no pollinating agent or partner is needed, and that seedless varieties can still be multiplied (2 marks)
Disadvantage: there is no genetic variation, so the whole crop is equally vulnerable to a new disease or pest; accept also overcrowding and competition near the parent (2 marks)
questions.explanation: The four differences are clearest when written as matched pairs. The agricultural advantages of vegetative propagation follow from genetic uniformity and speed, and the disadvantage follows from the same uniformity, since a clone population has no resistant individuals to survive a new disease.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a method of asexual reproduction that involves the division of a parent organism into two or more parts?
questions.explanation: Fission is a method of asexual reproduction where an organism divides into two or more parts, each of which can develop into a new individual. This method is common in unicellular organisms like bacteria and protozoa.

distractorRationale.a: Budding involves the formation of a new organism from a bud on the parent organism, not division.
distractorRationale.c: Fragmentation involves breaking into pieces, but the question specifically asks for division into parts.
distractorRationale.d: Spore formation is a different asexual method where spores are produced, not division.
